the land that you are entering to possess is a land unclean with the pollutions of the people of the lands, with their abominations. They have filled it from end to end with their uncleanness. Therefore, do not give your daughters to their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons, and never seek their peace or propriety, so that you may be strong and eat the good of the land and leave it for an inheritance to your children forever.

After all that has come upon us for our evil deeds and for our great guilt, seeing that you, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities deserved, and have given us such a remnant at this, shall we break your commandment again, and intermarry with the people who practice these abominations? Would you not be angry with us until you destroy us with no remnant or survivor?

God of Israel, you are just, but we have escaped as a remnant, as is now the case. Here we are before you in our guilt, though no one can face you because of this.

The Jews of Persia are not the same as the Israelites of David. As you can see from this map, the Jews are in this area and it's a very small part of the Levant, but it's a part of the Levant that's completely loyal to Persia because they see everyone else as unclean, as the enemy. If you're an empire, having the Jews around are really good for you.

The Jews are an invention of the Persians, but guess what? The nation of Israel is also an invention of the British Empire. So we move on to the second book called Nehemiah. Ezra is the priest who will create the Bible. Nehemiah is the governor sent by the Persians to reestablish the Jewish nation.

At the time I was cupbearer to the king, which is like a really powerful position because you can poison the king. In the month of Nissan in the 20th year of King Artaxerxes when wine was served him, I carried the wine and gave it to the king. Now I had never been sad in this presence before. So the king said to me, "Why is your face sad since you are not sick? This can only be sadness of the heart." Then I was very much afraid. I said to the king, "May the king live forever. Why should my face not be sad when the city, the place of my ancestors' graves, lies waste and its gates have been destroyed by fire?"
